title: I Enforced the Public-Piano Slot Clock on the Busker Who Booked Ghost Hours

parts.text: I reserved 12:00–12:30 on the station piano and at 12:02 a busker named Kade was still on the bench with a hat. The plaque said: RESERVE THE SLOT. THIRTY MINUTES. NO GHOST HOLDS. I was twenty-five, lunch player, holding a QR. Kade kept playing. "Hats are reservations of the people." I photographed the plaque, the QR, and the hat on my time. Then I logged a ghost hold. At 12:09 transit arts asked why Kade's hat was on my slot. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Transit arts can see Kade's hat on my 12:00 QR against the thirty-minute plaque.

social.video_title: He kept the piano on a ghost hold through my slot — Part 1/2
social.description: Station piano, a hat, and a plaque slot I reserved. I logged the ghost. Would you have shown the QR?

parts.text: Kade called it a crowd until arts asked for the log. I printed the ghost, the photo, and the QR. The bench opened. Kade reserved a real slot and told the concourse hats were always about optics. Optics is a word buskers use when a hat exists. Clock policy now has a second line: HATS ARE NOT HOLDS. I keep my thirty. Kade books. The piano finally sounds like a slot, not a lease. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Ghost-hold log, open bench, and a second line. Was a crowd ever my QR?
